findings.explanation: The Meraki uplinks loss and latency API is documented for MX appliances; cameras may never appear in it, in which case the search returns no camera rows. Check the API documentation and sample events for MV serials.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm MV devices report in this sourcetype; otherwise use another signal (availability, webhook alerts) and say so.

findings.explanation: The data source states no per-camera quality score exists; the search outputs loss and latency and a derived label.
findings.quote: Quality score gauge per camera; quality trend line; affected camera list.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe a table of cameras with loss, latency and stream_health, plus a loss/latency trend.

findings.explanation: The availabilities sourcetype is listed as a source, but the SPL never uses it and has no camera filter, so any device type in the loss and latency feed would appear.
findings.suggested_fix: Either join camera availability into the search (human edit) or remove it from the data sources and add a note on scoping to MV serials.

findings.explanation: The 1% and 100 ms thresholds are presented as fact without any source; the same applies to the alert name 'Camera unable to upload to cloud', which is unconfirmed.
findings.quote: Loss > 1% or latency > 100ms generally degrades cloud video continuity.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark thresholds as starting points to tune, and confirm alert names in the Dashboard.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: 'Video Quality Score' overstates what is measured; the SPL derives network-path health, not video quality.
The case() final true() branch is unreachable after the where filter, and `network.name` may not exist on the loss/latency events.

summary: Candidly says the TA has no quality score, yet the title and visualization promise one. The SPL uses an uplink loss and latency sourcetype that may not carry camera data, and does not filter to cameras.
